blocks.text: iOS 12 emphasized responsiveness across the supported device range and introduced major user-facing systems for Screen Time, grouped notifications, Siri Shortcuts, shared augmented reality, Memoji, and richer Photos discovery.

citations.locator: iOS 12 — Performance, Photos, Messages, Screen Time, Notifications, Siri, and Augmented Reality
Faster and More Responsive through Siri Shortcuts

blocks.text: The release also tightened Safari tracking defenses and password handling, expanded Core ML and networking capabilities for developers, and shipped a broad security bulletin covering system, app, media, web, and device-access components.

citations.locator: Core ML, Networking, and USB Accessories

blocks.text: iOS 12.0.1 was an early maintenance release for charging and Wi-Fi behavior on iPhone XS, the iPad symbol-key layout, video subtitles, and Bluetooth availability.
Its security bulletin separately records two lock-screen access problems involving VoiceOver and Quick Look, both addressed by restricting the options available while a device was locked.

citations.locator: VoiceOver — CVE-2018-4380 and Quick Look — CVE-2018-4379

blocks.text: iOS 12.1 delivered Group FaceTime for as many as 32 participants, more than 70 emoji, Dual SIM with eSIM on the 2018 iPhone family, and real-time Depth Control in supported Portrait-mode previews.

citations.locator: iOS 12.1 — Group FaceTime, Emoji, Dual SIM support, and other improvements
Group FaceTime, New Emoji, Depth Control, and Dual SIM

blocks.text: The update also added Screen Time authentication controls and performance management on additional iPhones, corrected several communications and reporting issues, documented an AR Quick Look compatibility issue, and carried a separate multi-component security bulletin.
iOS 12.1.1 expanded notification previews on iPhone XR, eSIM carrier support, FaceTime camera and Live Photo controls, real-time text calling, and stability for dictation and VoiceOver.

Apple also fixed Face ID, voicemail, Messages keyboard, Voice Memos, and time-zone problems; its developer note added a Certificate Transparency requirement for newly issued publicly trusted TLS certificates, while the security bulletin covered additional component fixes.
iOS 12.1.2 was an iPhone-focused maintenance release that corrected eSIM activation on iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max and addressed cellular connectivity for those models in Türkiye.

Apple’s 2018–2019 security index lists the release date and explicitly states that iOS 12.1.2 has no published CVE entries, so this record does not infer any security detail beyond Apple’s disclosure.

citations.locator: iOS 12.1.2 — no published CVE entries; released December 17, 2018

blocks.text: iOS 12.1.3 fixed photo browsing in Messages, image artifacts after Share Sheet use, external-audio distortion on 2018 iPad Pro models, and CarPlay disconnections on the 2018 iPhone family.

The release also corrected HomePod restarts and Siri listening failures, and Apple published a separate security bulletin covering AppleKeyStore, Bluetooth, FaceTime, kernel, web, and other components.

iOS 12.2 launched Apple News+ in the United States and Canada and added Siri video playback on Apple TV, four Animoji, expanded AirPlay controls, Screen Time scheduling, AirPods 2 support, and several Wallet and Safari changes.

citations.locator: iOS 12.2 — Apple News+, Siri, Animoji, AirPlay, Apple Pay, Screen Time, Safari, and AirPods

blocks.text: For developers, StoreKit added subscription offers and HealthKit exposed several heart-notification sample types as read-only data. Apple’s security bulletin separately documents fixes across networking, media, kernel, Safari, WebKit, and other components.

citations.locator: App Store — Promoting Your Subscriptions with New Offers; HealthKit — New Features

blocks.text: iOS 12.3 paired AirPlay 2-enabled smart-TV playback with a redesigned Apple TV app offering channels, downloads, family sharing, recommendations, purchasing, rentals, and a dedicated children’s section.

citations.locator: iOS 12.3 — AirPlay 2 and Apple TV app
Apple TV channels, Family Sharing, Kids, and AirPlay 2 availability

blocks.text: The update also changed Apple News+ and Apple Music discovery, disabled insecure Bluetooth accessories, fixed several remote and call failures, added Japanese Reiwa-era calendar support, and carried an extensive security bulletin.
iOS 12.3.1 was a focused maintenance release for VoLTE calling and two Messages behaviors involving filtered unknown senders and the Report Junk link.
Apple’s security index explicitly lists the release as having no published CVE entries, so the record stays limited to the three consumer-facing fixes Apple identified.

citations.locator: iOS 12.3.1 — no published CVE entries; released May 24, 2019

blocks.text: iOS 12.4 introduced direct wireless iPhone-to-iPhone migration during setup and revised Apple News+ issue access, publication browsing, and downloaded-issue cleanup.

citations.locator: iOS 12.4 — iPhone migration and Apple News

blocks.text: The release re-enabled Apple Watch Walkie-Talkie after a security fix, added HomePod support in Japan and Taiwan, corrected a false-positive issue in the Leaks developer instrument, and shipped a separate multi-component security bulletin.

citations.locator: iOS 12.4 — Other improvements and fixes; HomePod support

blocks.text: Apple described iOS 12.4.1 as a recommended security and stability update without listing separate consumer-facing features or ordinary bug fixes.
The security bulletin identifies one kernel use-after-free vulnerability that could let a malicious application execute code with system privileges, addressed through improved memory management.

events.summary: The public iOS 12 release combined broad performance work with new photo discovery, communication, wellbeing, automation, augmented-reality, privacy, developer, and device-access capabilities.

changes.title: System performance improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple tuned system responsiveness and app, keyboard, and camera launch behavior across the supported hardware range.
changes.summary: iOS 12 focused on faster everyday interactions across supported devices extending back to iPhone 5s and iPad Air, including app launches, keyboard appearance, typing, and Camera access.

changes.title: Photos discovery and sharing
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos gained a For You destination, sharing suggestions, richer search, faster import previews, and RAW editing support.
changes.summary: A new For You tab surfaced featured memories and effect ideas, sharing suggestions connected event participants, and search could combine intelligent terms such as people, places, businesses, and events.

citations.locator: Photos For You and More Ways to Search

changes.title: Memoji and Messages camera effects
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages added customizable Memoji, additional Animoji and expression tracking, and real-time camera effects.
changes.summary: Users could create personalized Memoji, use new Animoji characters with wink and tongue detection, and apply Animoji, filters, text, stickers, and shapes while capturing Messages photos and videos.

changes.title: Screen Time
changes.canonicalSummary: Screen Time added usage reporting, app and website limits, and family controls for children’s device activity.
changes.summary: Screen Time summarized app and website activity, notifications, and device pickups; App Limits constrained selected use, while Family Sharing let parents view reports and manage a child’s schedule.

citations.locator: Screen Time, Do Not Disturb and Notifications

changes.title: Grouped notifications and expanded Do Not Disturb
changes.canonicalSummary: Notification grouping and lock-screen delivery controls arrived alongside time-, place-, event-, and bedtime-based Do Not Disturb modes.
changes.summary: Notifications from an app could be grouped and tuned directly from the Lock Screen, including quiet delivery, while Do Not Disturb gained automatic ending conditions and a Bedtime presentation.

citations.locator: iOS 12 — Do Not Disturb and Notifications
Screen Time, Do Not Disturb and Notifications

changes.title: Siri Shortcuts
changes.canonicalSummary: Apps could expose routine actions to Siri, and users could run suggested or custom shortcuts by voice.
changes.summary: Supported apps gained Add to Siri actions, the system suggested shortcuts based on routines, and the Shortcuts app let users assemble multi-step voice-triggered workflows.

changes.title: ARKit 2 and Measure
changes.canonicalSummary: Augmented reality gained shared and persistent experiences, object and image tracking, systemwide Quick Look, and a measuring app.
changes.summary: ARKit 2 supported shared sessions, saved experiences, moving-image tracking, and AR Quick Look in Apple apps, while Measure used augmented reality to estimate lines, surfaces, and rectangular objects.

changes.title: Safari tracking and password protections
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari reduced cross-site tracking and fingerprinting while the system improved password generation, reuse warnings, code autofill, and credential sharing.
changes.summary: Enhanced Intelligent Tracking Prevention limited tracking by embedded social controls and reduced device fingerprinting, while strong-password suggestions, reuse flags, SMS security-code AutoFill, and AirDrop password sharing strengthened account workflows.

changes.title: Core ML model and prediction expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: Core ML added quantized, flexible-shape, batch, custom, and Create ML model support.
changes.summary: The iOS 12 SDK expanded Core ML with compact quantized models, flexible input shapes, batch prediction, custom layers, and models trained through Create ML templates.

changes.title: Locked-device USB accessory protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Passcode-protected devices could require an unlock before communicating with computers or USB accessories.
changes.summary: iOS 12 could block data communication and some accessory behavior over USB until the device was unlocked, with a separate accessibility setting available for assistive USB devices.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.0.1 release corrected five early charging, Wi-Fi, keyboard, media, and Bluetooth problems and fixed two separately documented lock-screen access vulnerabilities.

changes.title: iPhone XS Lightning charging fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected iPhone XS devices began charging promptly when connected to a Lightning cable.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition in which some iPhone XS devices did not immediately start charging after a Lightning cable was attached.

changes.title: iPhone XS Wi-Fi band fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected iPhone XS devices could rejoin a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network instead of falling back to 2.4 GHz.
changes.summary: The update resolved an iPhone XS reconnection issue that could select the 2.4 GHz band instead of the available 5 GHz Wi-Fi network.

changes.title: iPad symbol-key position restoration
changes.canonicalSummary: The iPad keyboard restored the symbol-switching key to its earlier position.
changes.summary: Apple returned the “.?123” key on the iPad keyboard to its original location.

changes.title: Subtitle and Bluetooth availability fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Video subtitles appeared in the affected apps and Bluetooth remained available in the documented failure state.
changes.summary: The maintenance release addressed missing subtitles in some video apps and a separate condition that could make Bluetooth unavailable.

changes.title: VoiceOver lock-screen access fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Restricted lock-screen options prevented a local attacker from using VoiceOver to view photos and contacts.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2018-4380 by limiting VoiceOver options available while the device was locked, closing access to photos and contacts in the documented scenario.

changes.title: Quick Look lock-screen sharing fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Restricted lock-screen options prevented a local attacker from opening the share function through Quick Look.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2018-4379 by limiting Quick Look options on a locked device so the share function was not exposed in the documented path.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.1 release introduced Group FaceTime, new emoji, Dual SIM, live Depth Control, additional Screen Time and battery controls, and targeted reliability and security corrections.

changes.title: Group FaceTime
changes.canonicalSummary: FaceTime added end-to-end encrypted audio and video conversations for groups of up to 32 participants.
changes.summary: Users could start or join a Group FaceTime session from FaceTime or a group Messages conversation, with automatic speaker prominence and support for as many as 32 participants.

changes.title: More than 70 new emoji
changes.canonicalSummary: The emoji keyboard expanded with new people, expressions, animals, sports, food, and other symbols.
changes.summary: iOS 12.1 added more than 70 emoji, including additional hair representation, faces, animals, sports, food, travel, and cultural symbols.

changes.title: Dual SIM with eSIM
changes.canonicalSummary: The 2018 iPhone family gained support for two cellular numbers through a nano-SIM and eSIM combination.
changes.summary: iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR could activate an additional carrier plan through eSIM while retaining a physical nano-SIM line.

changes.title: Live Depth Control preview
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported iPhones could adjust Portrait-mode depth of field before capture as well as afterward.
changes.summary: Depth Control became available in the live Camera preview on iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR, extending the existing post-capture adjustment workflow.

changes.title: Screen Time passcode authentication
changes.canonicalSummary: Parents could use Face ID or Touch ID when changing or resetting a child’s Screen Time passcode.
changes.summary: Screen Time added biometric authentication to the workflow for changing or resetting a child’s Screen Time passcode.

changes.title: Messages, voicemail, Phone, and reporting fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: A grouped maintenance pass corrected merged message threads, missing voicemail and contact names, incomplete Screen Time reporting, and Family Sharing changes.
changes.summary: Apple fixed conversations merged across shared Apple IDs, absent voicemails and Phone contact names, missing website activity in Screen Time, and failures adding or removing Family Sharing members.

changes.title: VoiceOver lock-screen photo access fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved state management blocked a local attacker from viewing photos through a locked device’s reply workflow.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2018-4387, a VoiceOver-related path that could expose photos through Reply With Message while the device remained locked.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.1.1 release expanded notification, eSIM, FaceTime, RTT, and HomePod behavior, corrected several reliability problems, and introduced a stricter TLS certificate policy.

changes.title: iPhone XR Haptic Touch notification previews
changes.canonicalSummary: iPhone XR users could open notification previews through Haptic Touch.
changes.summary: Notification previews became available through a Haptic Touch press on iPhone XR.

changes.title: Expanded eSIM carrier support
changes.canonicalSummary: Dual SIM with eSIM became compatible with additional carriers on the 2018 iPhone family.
changes.summary: Apple expanded eSIM carrier availability for iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max.

changes.title: FaceTime camera switching and Live Photos
changes.canonicalSummary: FaceTime added one-tap camera switching and restored Live Photo capture for one-to-one calls.
changes.summary: Participants could switch between rear and front cameras with one tap and capture a Live Photo during an individual FaceTime call.

changes.title: RTT calling and accessibility stability
changes.canonicalSummary: Real-time text calling expanded to Wi-Fi calling on iPad and iPod touch, while dictation and VoiceOver stability improved.
changes.summary: The update enabled RTT over Wi-Fi calling on iPad and iPod touch and improved stability for dictation and VoiceOver.

changes.title: Face ID, voicemail, Messages, and Voice Memos fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: A grouped maintenance pass corrected temporary Face ID loss, voicemail downloads, predictive text, Voice Memos uploads, and automatic time zones.
changes.summary: Apple addressed temporary Face ID unavailability, visual voicemail download failures, missing Chinese or Japanese keyboard suggestions in Messages, blocked Voice Memos iCloud uploads, and stale time zones.

changes.title: HomePod regional support and Group FaceTime indicators
changes.canonicalSummary: HomePod expanded to China mainland and Hong Kong and illuminated its LEDs during Group FaceTime calls.
changes.summary: The companion HomePod portion added regional support for China mainland and Hong Kong and used the device LEDs during Group FaceTime sessions.

changes.title: TLS Certificate Transparency requirement
changes.canonicalSummary: Newly issued publicly trusted TLS server certificates had to satisfy Apple’s Certificate Transparency policy to be trusted.
changes.summary: iOS 12.1.1 required publicly trusted TLS server-authentication certificates issued after October 15, 2018 to meet Apple’s Certificate Transparency policy before the platform would evaluate them as trusted.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.1.2 release was a focused iPhone maintenance update for eSIM activation and cellular connectivity.

citations.locator: iOS 12.1.2 — released December 17, 2018; no published CVE entries

changes.title: eSIM activation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A documented activation problem was corrected for eSIM service on the 2018 iPhone family.
changes.summary: Apple fixed an issue that could prevent eSIM activation on iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max.

changes.title: Türkiye cellular connectivity fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Cellular connectivity reliability improved for the 2018 iPhone family in Türkiye.
changes.summary: The update addressed a cellular connectivity problem affecting iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max in Türkiye.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.1.3 release concentrated on Messages, Photos sharing, iPad Pro audio, CarPlay, and HomePod reliability, alongside published security corrections.

changes.title: Messages photo browsing fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos displayed from a Messages conversation could be browsed without the documented scrolling problem.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition that could disrupt scrolling through photos from the Details view of a Messages conversation.

changes.title: Photo Share Sheet artifact fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos sent through the Share Sheet no longer showed the documented striped visual artifacts.
changes.summary: The release addressed striped artifacts that could appear in photos after they were sent from the Share Sheet.

changes.title: 2018 iPad Pro external audio fix
changes.canonicalSummary: External audio input no longer produced the documented distortion on the 2018 iPad Pro.
changes.summary: Apple corrected audio distortion that could occur when external audio input devices were used with 2018 iPad Pro models.

citations.locator: iOS 12.1.3 — iPad Pro external audio input

changes.title: CarPlay disconnection fix
changes.canonicalSummary: The 2018 iPhone family maintained CarPlay connections more reliably.
changes.summary: The update addressed unexpected CarPlay disconnections on iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max.

changes.title: HomePod restart and Siri listening fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: HomePod stability improved for unexpected restarts and a condition that could interrupt Siri listening.
changes.summary: The companion HomePod update addressed unexpected restarts and a separate issue that could cause Siri to stop listening.

changes.title: AppleKeyStore sandbox restriction fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Additional sandbox restrictions prevented a malicious application from bypassing documented key-store restrictions.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2019-6235 by adding sandbox restrictions around AppleKeyStore behavior exposed to a malicious application.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.2 release launched Apple News+, expanded Siri and AirPlay television controls, added new Animoji and AirPods support, refined Screen Time, Wallet, and Safari, and introduced new developer capabilities.

changes.title: Apple News+
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple News added a subscription catalog of magazines and selected newspapers in the United States and Canada.
changes.summary: Apple News+ launched inside the News app with magazine and selected newspaper access for subscribers in the United States and Canada.

changes.title: Siri video playback on Apple TV
changes.canonicalSummary: Siri on iPhone and iPad could request playback of supported video content on Apple TV.
changes.summary: Users could ask Siri on an iPhone or iPad to play supported movies, shows, sports, channels, or genres on Apple TV.

changes.title: Four new Animoji
changes.canonicalSummary: The Animoji collection expanded with owl, boar, giraffe, and shark characters.
changes.summary: Messages and FaceTime added owl, boar, giraffe, and shark Animoji on supported devices.

changes.title: AirPlay television controls and multitasking
changes.canonicalSummary: Control Center and the Lock Screen gained dedicated television controls, while local app use could continue during AirPlay video sessions.
changes.summary: AirPlay added faster access to television controls and allowed users to browse other apps or play short local media without interrupting streamed video.

changes.title: Apple Pay Cash and Wallet refinements
changes.canonicalSummary: Wallet added transaction detail and easier Apple Pay Cash balance actions, including instant bank transfer where available.
changes.summary: Apple Pay Cash customers could transfer funds instantly to eligible Visa debit cards and use redesigned Wallet views for balance actions and transaction details.

changes.title: Per-day Screen Time scheduling
changes.canonicalSummary: Downtime schedules could vary by weekday and app limits could be toggled temporarily.
changes.summary: Screen Time added separate Downtime schedules for each day and an option to turn app limits on or off temporarily.

changes.title: Safari password and privacy changes
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari strengthened password workflows and site warnings while changing its tracking-prevention controls.
changes.summary: Safari expanded Password AutoFill, warned on unencrypted web pages that requested credentials or payment information, strengthened cross-site tracking prevention, and removed the obsolete Do Not Track setting.

changes.title: Second-generation AirPods support
changes.canonicalSummary: iOS added compatibility with the second generation of AirPods.
changes.summary: The release added system support for second-generation AirPods.

changes.title: StoreKit subscription offers
changes.canonicalSummary: Developers could present discounted subscription offers to current and former subscribers.
changes.summary: StoreKit added subscription offers, allowing eligible customers with an active or expired auto-renewable subscription to receive developer-configured discounts.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.3 release brought AirPlay 2 television support and a redesigned Apple TV app, refined News and Music, tightened accessory security, corrected connectivity and display problems, and added Japanese calendar support for the Reiwa era.

changes.title: AirPlay 2 smart television support
changes.canonicalSummary: Compatible smart televisions could receive videos, photos, music, and other content through AirPlay 2.
changes.summary: iPhone and iPad could stream or share supported media directly to AirPlay 2-enabled smart televisions.

changes.title: Redesigned Apple TV app and Channels
changes.canonicalSummary: The Apple TV app introduced a new discovery experience, Apple TV Channels subscriptions, family sharing, and a dedicated children’s area.
changes.summary: The redesigned TV app combined personalized recommendations with direct channel subscriptions, Family Sharing access, and an editorially selected Kids section.

citations.locator: Apple TV Channels, Family Sharing, and Kids

changes.title: News+ and Music discovery refinements
changes.canonicalSummary: News+ improved magazine following and Music refreshed its personalized recommendations more frequently.
changes.summary: Apple News+ added catalog follow controls and Apple Music’s For You area began updating recommendations multiple times each day.

citations.locator: iOS 12.3 — Apple News+ and Apple Music

changes.title: Insecure Bluetooth accessory connections disabled
changes.canonicalSummary: Bluetooth accessories using connections Apple identified as insecure were blocked from connecting.
changes.summary: The release disabled connections to Bluetooth accessories that relied on insecure connection behavior.

changes.title: Remote, Wi-Fi Calling, and vehicle display fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: A grouped maintenance pass improved Apple TV Remote responsiveness, Wi-Fi Calling stability, and song metadata shown by vehicle displays.
changes.summary: Apple addressed an unresponsive Apple TV Remote, dropped Wi-Fi Calling, and missing song information on some vehicle displays.

changes.title: Reiwa Japanese calendar era
changes.canonicalSummary: Foundation and related date handling gained support for the Reiwa era of the Japanese calendar.
changes.summary: The platform added support for the Reiwa era in Japanese calendar calculations and date formatting.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.3.1 release was a narrow maintenance update for VoLTE calls and two Messages filtering and reporting behaviors.

citations.locator: iOS 12.3.1 — released May 24, 2019; no published CVE entries

changes.title: VoLTE call reliability fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Calls using Voice over LTE no longer encountered the documented connection or disconnection problem.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition that could prevent VoLTE calls from being made or received.

changes.title: Unknown sender filtering fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages from unknown senders were filtered when the setting was enabled.
changes.summary: The update addressed a Messages issue that could allow unknown-sender messages into the main conversation list despite filtering being enabled.

changes.title: Messages Report Junk link fix
changes.canonicalSummary: The Report Junk link appeared for eligible conversations from unknown senders.
changes.summary: Apple restored the Report Junk link when viewing a Messages thread from an unknown sender.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.4 release introduced wireless iPhone migration, expanded Apple News+ library controls, restored Walkie-Talkie after a security correction, added HomePod regional support, and corrected developer tooling.

changes.title: Wireless iPhone migration
changes.canonicalSummary: Setup could transfer data directly from an existing iPhone to a nearby new iPhone without a wired connection.
changes.summary: Quick Start added a wireless device-to-device migration path for moving data from an old iPhone during setup.

changes.title: Apple News+ downloaded issues and catalog
changes.canonicalSummary: News+ kept downloaded magazine issues available in My Magazines and exposed all publications in a browsable catalog.
changes.summary: Downloaded magazine issues became accessible online and offline from My Magazines, and a catalog made the News+ publication lineup easier to browse.

citations.locator: iOS 12.4 — Apple News+ downloaded issues and catalog

changes.title: Apple News+ download removal controls
changes.canonicalSummary: News+ users could remove downloaded magazine issues through History.
changes.summary: The News app added a Clear option in History for deleting downloaded magazine issues.

changes.title: Walkie-Talkie security correction
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple corrected a security problem in the Apple Watch Walkie-Talkie app and restored the feature.
changes.summary: The Walkie-Talkie feature returned after Apple addressed the security issue that had led it to be disabled.

changes.title: HomePod support for Japan and Taiwan
changes.canonicalSummary: HomePod gained regional support for Japan and Taiwan.
changes.summary: The companion HomePod software expanded regional availability to Japan and Taiwan.

changes.title: Leaks instrument false-positive correction
changes.canonicalSummary: The Leaks instrument stopped reporting a documented class of false-positive leaks for iOS applications.
changes.summary: Apple corrected an Instruments issue that could cause the Leaks tool to report false positives while profiling iOS apps.

events.summary: The public iOS 12.4.1 release was a security-focused maintenance update whose published bulletin documents a kernel use-after-free correction.

changes.title: Kernel use-after-free fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved memory management addressed a kernel use-after-free that could allow an application to execute code with system privileges.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2019-8605, a kernel memory-safety issue that could let a malicious application gain system privileges.
